findings.scene: scenes 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, 10 (scene-03-square.js, scene-04-arrow.js, scene-05-table.js, scene-07-leak.js, scene-09-split.js, scene-10-halve.js)
findings.problem: Numbers are typed into captions and tags instead of coming from the asserted helpers (house rule: numbers come from the helpers and are asserted, never typed). Scene 3 CAPS lines 48-49 'Add a weaker wave, 3 times faster.' / 'Then 5 times faster...' (SQ.freq(2) and SQ.freq(3) exist and are asserted, the strings are not tied to them). Scene 4 line 46 'Take 8 samples of a wave.', line 127 tag '8 samples', lines 140 and 191 'test: 1 spin' / 'test: 2 spins' (the k of A9.chain(k)). Scene 5 line 64 'Each test reads all 8 samples.' (while the neighbouring captions and tags do use N and W8.products, so the scene mixes both styles). Scene 7 lines 184 and 188-189 '8 whole cycles' / '8.5 cycles' although A9.LEAK.whole and A9.LEAK.half hold exactly these numbers. Scene 9 is entirely typed: captions lines 55, 57, 59 ('all 64 products', 'cost 16 each', '32 products and 4 butterflies, not 64') and tags lines 303-304, 409, 417 ('64 products', 'was 64 products', '2 x 16 = 32 products', '32 + 4 butterflies'); check() asserts FF.products / FF.half / FF.split but never compares them with these strings, so the text can drift from the numbers without any error. Scene 10 captions lines 60-63 ('12 butterflies', '18 minutes or 0.02 seconds', 'About 50,000 times less work') are typed although the matching on-screen tags and the red bar are built from COST / FF (lines 188, 193, 210, 218, 309), so caption and picture can disagree after an edit. The numbers are all correct today; the problem is that nothing guards them.
findings.fix: Build every number in a caption or tag from the helper that owns it, and keep the existing assertions: scene 3 `${SQ.freq(2)} times faster` and `${SQ.freq(3)} times faster`; scene 4 `Take ${X.length} samples of a wave.`, tag `${X.length} samples`, `test: ${r} spin${r > 1 ? 's' : ''}`; scene 5 `Each test reads all ${N} samples.`; scene 7 `${LK.whole} whole cycles` and `${LK.half} cycles`; scene 9 `${FF.products}`, `${FF.half}`, `${FF.split.products}`, `${FF.split.butterflies}`; scene 10 `${FF.butterflies}`, `${Math.round(COST.directMin)} minutes`, `${COST.fftSec.toFixed(2)} seconds`, `${A9.commas(Math.round(COST.ratio / 1e4) * 1e4)}`. Where a caption has to stay a literal sentence, add one A9.same(...) in check() that the caption string contains String(helper value).
findings.evidence: Source lines listed above (grep for the digits in CAPS and A9.tag calls). The only caption numbers that are already derived are scene 5's `${N} x ${N} = ${W8.products}` and scene 6's A.fs / A.twin / A.f / A.fold.

findings.problem: The payoff of the second run (spin twice: total 0, 'no match') is on screen for well under a second and without a caption, so the scene ends before it can be read. Timeline: the loop closes at 12.6 s, the origin ring 12.6-13.0, the 'total 0' card 12.8-13.2, the 'no match' tag 13.0-13.4; caption 5 ('The arrows loop back and cancel.') ends at 13.2 and the scene's 0.3 s fade-out starts at 13.7 (dur 14). Measured by comparing the scene DOM every 0.05 s: the last change is at 13.4 s, so the finished frame holds still for 0.3 s before the fade, and for the last 0.8 s of the scene there is no caption. Run 1's payoff (total 4, 'a match') also only lasts 0.4 s before it is cleared (8.2-8.8). The house rule is that each state sits about a second.
findings.fix: Either speed run 2 up (SWEEP[1].per 0.4 -> 0.3 so the loop closes at 11.8, and move ring / stat2 / nomatch and the caption 5 start 0.8 s earlier), or add about 1.2 s to the scene (dur 14 -> 15.2, total 125 -> 126.2 s, still under 130 s) and keep caption 5 up to 14.6 so the verdict has at least a second on screen with its caption before the fade. The check() that ties captions to pictures (starts[]) must follow the new times.
findings.evidence: Stills algo-9 s4@12.4 (loop closing, caption 'The arrows loop back and cancel.'), s4@13.6 (total 0 and 'no match' complete, no caption) and s4@13.9 (already fading). DOM-change scan: s4 lastChange 13.4, hold-before-fade 0.3 s; every other scene holds 1.25-2.5 s (scene 2: 0.4 s).

findings.problem: The un-lit lines of the FFT network are drawn in var(--line) (#e5e5e5), 4 px wide, which is only 1.26:1 against the white panel. Those lines are the thing scenes 9 and 10 explain (which rows a butterfly pairs, how the levels connect), and before a butterfly lights up they are the only trace of its wiring: scene 9 from 5.6 to 6.6 s and 8.0 to 9.4 s, scene 10 from 0.1 to 4.1 s (the whole 'split down to single samples' beat, where the grey lines are all that shows the structure being built) and again for the level-2 butterflies. On a phone-sized view a 1.26:1 line of that weight is close to invisible. The sticker palette has stronger greys for exactly this.
findings.fix: In fftRig's grey(...) use var(--line-2) (#d4d4d4, 1.48:1) at minimum, or var(--node-off-ic) (#afafaf, 2.19:1) which still reads as 'not yet computed' against the 6 px coloured overlay; keep the overlay colours as they are. Same for the grey connector strokes in scene-09-split.js line 393 (cn.base.style.stroke = var(--line)).
findings.evidence: Contrast computed from tokens-main.css (--line #e5e5e5 on #fff = 1.26, --line-2 = 1.48, --node-off-ic = 2.19). Stills algo-9 s9@6.0, s10@2.6 and s10@5.0 show the grey crossings as the faintest element on the stage next to much heavier tiles and tags.

findings.problem: The two tags in the top row collide when the sample-rate tag pulses. The rate tag is scaled by 1 + 0.08 x flash (lines 206-207) when 'half the sample rate' is named (5.7-6.2 s) and when it changes to '16 samples a second' (9.8-10.2 s). The pill is 311-346 px wide, so the 8 % growth moves its left edge 12-14 px to the left and it runs into the '7 Hz wave' tag beside it (rest gap 10 px).
findings.fix: Do the same as scenes 2 and 4 do for wide tags and use a hop (`y: -8 * flash(...)`) instead of a scale, or move TAG_X[1] from 190 to 204.
findings.evidence: DOM boxes every 0.25 s: gap between the two tags 5.6 px at 57.75 s, -2.2 px at 58.0 s (scene local 6.0) and -3.4 px at 62.0 s (local 10.0). Still algo-9 s6@6.0 shows the two pills touching.

findings.scene: scene-09-split.js (and the same swing in common-4.js R.tilesAt; scene-10-halve.js has a smaller version)
findings.problem: The input tiles pass over each other while they swap rows. R.tilesAt swings movers only 22 px sideways (its doc comment says 'so they never overlap'), but the tiles are 76 px wide and rows are 68 px apart, so in scene 9 the pairs x1/x2, x3/x4, x5/x6 (and x1/x4, x3/x6, x1/x6) overlap for 0.7 s (local 3.4 to 4.05) by up to 2,380 px2, about 60 % of a tile, one tile hiding the label of the other. Scene 10 already replaced the rig's swing by its own lanes (LANE 24 left / 60 right) and still overlaps x2/x4 and x3/x5 for 0.3 s (local 0.95 to 1.35) by up to 315 px2.
findings.fix: Give scene 9 the lanes scene 10 uses (about 24 px for tiles going up, 60 px for tiles going down), move the lane constants into R.tilesAt so both scenes share them, and widen the down lane a little more (about 70 px) so x2/x4 clear each other in scene 10.
findings.evidence: Still algo-9 s9@3.4 (x1 half behind x2, x3 behind x4, x5 behind x6), s10@1.0 (x4 over x2). Measured by intersecting the tile boxes every 0.05 s.

findings.problem: Several things sit flush against the stage edge, short of the house 12 px margin. The plot panels are 936 px wide from x 0 (scenes 2, 3, 4 right panel, 6, 7, 8), the scene 8 and scene 2/3 top panels start at stage y 0, and the first tag of scenes 4, 6 and 7 sits at stage (0, 0) (scene 4's 'sample x arrow, added' tag also at y 0 above a panel that ends at x 936). Bottom: scene 5's tags end at y 628.4 (11.6 px), scenes 9 and 10 bottom tag rows end at 626 and scene 10's butterfly counter card plus its 6 px lip reaches y 630 (10 px). Scene 10 part 2 starts its tags at x 12 and their pop overshoot reaches x 8-10. Nothing leaves the 1080 px canvas (the stage itself is 72 px in), and earlier phases (a3) use the same full-width panels, so this is only a rule-of-thumb break.
findings.fix: Optional: inset the shared panels to x 12..924 (w 912, keep pad.r) and start tag rows at y 12, or accept the full-width panels as the storyboard's layout (a3 did) and only fix the two bottom cases: scene 10's counter card y 570 -> 564 (so its lip ends at 624) and scene 5's tag row y 566 -> 564. The 626 px tag rows of scenes 9 and 10 already keep 14 px.
findings.evidence: Measured v-card / v-tag / v-gene rectangles every 0.25 s against the 936 x 640 stage: left 0 / right 936 / top 0 for the panels in scenes 2-4 and 6-8; 'bottom 626 + 6' for scenes 8-10; stills algo-9 s4@4.5, s6@4.0, s7@5.5.

findings.problem: Maths symbols are typed as text glyphs, while the recap (scene 11 sumRow) draws its plus and equals as SVG paths and the brand rule is symbols as SVG. The storyboard allows '+' and 'x' as text but not '='. '=' appears in 'row number = spins' (scene 5 tag), '8 x 8 = 64 products' (scene 5 tag and caption 4), '2 x 16 = 32 products' (scene 9 tag) and '1 sample = its own DFT' (scene 10 tag); 'x' in 'sample x arrow, added' (scene 4) and the axis ticks '1x ... 23x' (scene 3); '+' as a 52 px text between the two stacked waves in scene 2 and in '32 + 4 butterflies' (scene 9). Mixed rendering is also visible: scene 2's '+' is a halo-ed text glyph, the recap's is a drawn stroke.
findings.fix: Reword the '=' strings so no glyph is needed ('row number is the spin count', '1 sample is its own DFT'), or draw '=' and '+' with the small SVG strokes already written in scene-11-recap.js (move them into common-3.js as A9.plus / A9.equals). The '8 x 8 = 64' and '2 x 16 = 32' sums are the hard cases: either draw the '=' as two short SVG bars between the numbers or word them ('64 products: 8 by 8', '32 products: 2 halves of 16'). Leave 'x' on the axis ticks (it is a unit there).
findings.evidence: On-screen strings listed per scene by reading every visible text node every 0.25 s; same precedent flagged in the a7 brand review.
